options.description: What to offer. A string is a choice with that label, which has no key and so needs `numbered`. A heading is drawn when the list is, and is not in the `expand` line.
options.name: choices

options.description: Asks with plain lines in and lines out rather than a region that redraws, for a screen reader: the question is written once, what is typed is echoed where it is typed, and nothing already written is ever moved or erased.
options.name: accessible

options.description: Whether Escape leaves the prompt to go back a step. Defaults to `false`, where Escape does nothing, as it always has.
options.name: back

options.description: Show `(y/n/a/d/h)` instead of the list, and the list only once `h` or `?` is pressed. Both are kept for that, so a choice may not use either.
options.name: expand

options.description: The key Enter answers with, which is marked in the list and capitalised in the `expand` line. Without one Enter does nothing, as there is nothing highlighted for it to take.
options.name: initial

options.description: Give each choice that has no `key` its place in the list as one, from `1`. A choice past the ninth has no single digit to be and needs a key of its own.
options.name: numbered

options.description: The input router to read keys through. One is built if not given.
options.name: router

options.description: Gives the prompt up when this aborts, the way Ctrl-C does.
options.name: signal

options.description: Where keys come from. Defaults to the terminal's input.
options.name: stdin

options.description: An answer to start from: the choice whose `value` this is becomes the one Enter answers with, and beats `initial`. Compared the way a `Map` compares keys, and dropped -- leaving `initial` to decide -- when no choice on offer holds it.
options.name: value

registryDescription: A select-by-key prompt: press a choice's key, number the choices, or expand a compact line
